key_insight: Introduce an intent-controlled partial optimal transport framework that allows selective, pointwise rejection of mass based on side-specific reliability or external intent, instead of global scalar or budget-based rejections. This enables structured, interpretable partial matchings tailored to application-specific signals.
problem_solved: Standard partial OT enforces global or uniform rejection rules that cannot model pointwise differences in reliability or external directives, limiting usability in settings where some source/target components should be preferentially matched or left unmatched.
method: Formalize partial OT with intent: incorporate pointwise rejection decisions driven by side-specific reliability scores, geometric support, or external intent signals, replacing global budget/rebate rules.
Define a loss/constraint that couples matching with per-point rejection indicators so that mass can be selectively left unmatched according to intent while preserving OT structure.
Solve the resulting problem with scalable numerical routines by adapting existing OT solvers (e.g., regularized/iterative transport algorithms) to handle the added pointwise rejection terms.
impact: Provides practitioners a flexible, interpretable mechanism to enforce selective matching—useful for robust domain adaptation, outlier-aware alignment, and applications where side information or user intent should control which elements get matched.
visual_elements: Schematic before/after diagram: two point clouds with arrows showing standard OT matching vs. intent-controlled partial OT with selective rejections (crossed arrows).
Heatmap or color-coded support showing per-point reliability/intent scores that drive rejections.
Flowchart of the method: intent inputs → modified OT formulation → adapted solver → selective transport output.
Bar/chart comparing metrics (matching quality, rejection precision, runtime) between global partial OT and intent-controlled partial OT on a toy dataset.
paper_title: Take It or Leave It: Intent-Controlled Partial Optimal Transport
paper_authors: Salil Parth Tripathi, Bertrand Chapron, Fabrice Collard, Nicolas Courty, Ronan Fablet
